newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Adams says N.Irish bomb shows need for dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Adams says N.Irish bomb shows need for dialogue.

text.p: Gerry Adams, leader of the IRA's Sinn Fein political wing, said on Monday the bomb blast at Britain's Northern Ireland army base showed the need for all-party peace talks. In a statement to Irish media he said the blasts "emphasise the urgent need to fill the current protracted and dangerous vacuum with a process of real, inclusive dialogue."
Adams said it was too soon to say which organisation was responsible for the two bombs, which injured some 20 people, at least two critically.
"Obviously it is very regrettable that people have been injured," his statement said.

Sinn Fein is excluded from Anglo-Irish peace talks in Belfast because of the Irish Republican Army's decision to end a 17-month ceasefire and return to war in February against British rule of the province.
Spokesman for Northern Ireland political parties representing the 60 percent pro-British majority have accused the Irish Republican movement of carrying out the attack.
No group has claimed credit for the bombing, the first against a British security target in Northern Ireland since the IRA declared its ceasefire in August, 1994.

Northern Ireland peace talks have been under way since June grouping pro-british Unionist parties and the Social Democratic and Labour party of John Hume, a moderate, catholic-backed Irish nationalist group.

But they have failed to make any headway because of bickering about procedure and Unionist insistence that the negotiations lead directly to the disarmament of rival IRA and pro-british Loyalist groups.
